title: How to Conduct A/B Testing for Landing Pages
summary: A/B testing for landing pages is all about changing small variables to see which changes boost conversions. Do it right, and your sales can improve.
body_markdown:
A/B testing landing pages allows you to compare changes to a landing page so you can learn which variation encourages customers to take action. Toral Patel, senior vice president of marketing and ecommerce at the beauty brand Kopari, says on an episode of the[Shopify Masters podcast](https://www.shopify.com/blog/kopari-beauty-influencer-marketing-strategy) that the brand is “always testing. We’re trying to understand how to reduce friction and make sure we’re just making it an easy, simple process, so that somebody can convert really quickly.”


Toral is not alone in that mentality. In[Ascend2’s 2025 A/B Testing in Marketing](https://ascend2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/AB-Testing-in-Marketing-Research-Ascend2-250611.pdf) report, 32% of survey respondents said they use A/B landing page testing, and 53% named improving conversion rates as a primary objective.


Here’s more on A/B testing for landing pages, which elements to test, and how to run the testing process to support your conversion goals.


## What is A/B testing for landing pages?


[A/B testing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/the-complete-guide-to-ab-testing) , also known as split testing, involves creating different versions of a[landing page](https://www.shopify.com/blog/landing-page-optimization-tips) to see which performs better against a specific goal, like completing a purchase or signing up for a newsletter. Visitors are divided between the existing page (a control version) and a modified version that contains one isolated change.


Comparing conversion rates and other key metrics across the two landing page variations lets you make informed decisions about your page before rolling changes out more widely. For example, you could test two different headlines on a skincare product landing page—one leading with “Shop the new launch” and another with “Face washes for you”—then track clicks or purchases to see which performs better with your audience.


A/B tests are most effective when only a single element is different between the two pages. This allows you to clearly identify its effect on performance. Multivariable tests are possible, but with more changes in play, it’s harder to isolate each one’s contribution to the result, and harder to know which changes to carry forward into the control version of the page.

## What should you A/B test on landing pages?


- Page layout or element positioning
- Copy, text, and product information
- Images and media
- Calls to action (CTAs)
- Social proof
- Forms
- Navigation


Here’s a list of suggested landing page elements to test and what they measure:


### Page layout or element positioning


[Web page layout](https://www.shopify.com/blog/website-layout) is the arrangement of key page elements, including headlines, images,[call-to-action](https://www.shopify.com/blog/call-to-action-button-examples) (CTA) buttons, and sign-up forms. A/B testing can reveal how positioning affects shoppers’ ability to find what they need, interact with elements, and move on to further product pages.


To A/B test page layout, change one element’s position while leaving the rest of the page unchanged. For example, if your landing page includes a sign-up form, you could test one version with the form centered on the page against another with the form higher up near the fold, then see which version drives the higher sign-up rate.


### Copy, text, and product information


Text on your landing page may introduce your brand, describe your products or services, or help customers understand what they’ll find in your store. It can also guide them to other pages that go into more detail on specific product categories or individual items.


A/B testing can help you assess whether different wording holds visitors’ attention, gives a clear introduction to what you sell, and encourages customers to move beyond your landing page. You can test different headlines or product descriptions while keeping placement, design, font, and other features of the page unchanged.


For example, a cookware brand could compare two landing page headline variations: “Professional-grade stainless steel pans” versus “Cook restaurant-quality meals at home.” Comparing add-to-cart rates and purchases could reveal which messaging encourages shoppers to buy.


Shingly Lee of Guru[says on Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/guru-energy-customer-segmentation-marketing) , “If we’re going out with a campaign talking about a new product with a very clear A/B testing strategy, we’re able to tweak our digital platforms based on how well each campaign is converting and which consumer we want to speak to.”


### Images and media


Images and media are the pictures, videos, and visual content on your landing page. On a landing page, you can test your[hero image](https://www.shopify.com/blog/16480796-how-to-create-beautiful-and-persuasive-hero-images-for-your-online-store) , product images and videos, and marketing and lifestyle photos.


A sportswear brand could use a static image from its product catalog on one version and a dynamic video of clothing in use on another, then compare which version drives the most purchases.


### Calls to action (CTAs)


A call to action is a clickable link or button that urges users to perform a specific action, like viewing products or signing up for emails. Landing page CTAs direct visitors to the next step in your[sales funnel](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sales-funnel) , such as guiding them to a product page or encouraging them to start a free trial.


You can A/B test CTAs by changing single aspects like wording, color, or size. A clothing store might use “Shop now” on one version and “See the new collection” on another.


### Social proof


[Social proof](https://www.shopify.com/blog/social-proof) includes customer testimonials,[reviews](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-get-product-reviews) , ratings, and other details that help potential customers assess your business through other shoppers’ experiences. Compare a version of a landing page that includes a product-specific testimonial against a version without it. To evaluate the results, track visits to product pages, bounce rate, add-to-cart rates, or purchases.


### Forms


Landing page[forms](https://www.shopify.com/blog/shopify-forms) collect visitor information, such as contact details for mailing lists, or are used to share information, like downloadable product catalogs.


To A/B test a form, you can change the number of required fields to create a shorter and a longer version, then compare sign-up rates and form abandonment rates to learn whether form length affects completion. You can also track how many sign-ups from either version become purchasing customers to assess the quality of the leads each form generates.


### Navigation


Navigation includes the links, menus, and elements that take customers from your landing page to other site pages. You can test multiple variations in placement or the destinations navigation links point to. One version might include a link to a featured product collection, while another links to a homepage or hero product, keeping the link’s wording and placement unchanged.


Toral of Kopari encourages making popular products easy to find. “We have to make our top-selling products that we know resonate easy to navigate to,” she says. “We’re trying to understand how to reduce friction, and making sure we’re making it an easy, simple process so that somebody can convert quickly.”


## How to run A/B testing for landing pages


1. Review current performance and decide your goals
2. Decide what to test and form a hypothesis
3. Conduct your A/B test
4. Analyze your test results
5. Implement the winning version


Use these steps as a guide to start testing your own landing pages:


### 1. Review current performance and decide your goals


First, identify where sessions slow, pause, or stop progressing toward a purchase. Shopify store owners can use[conversion reports](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/behaviour-reports#online-store-conversion-over-time) to see how sessions progress from cart additions to checkout through to completed purchases.


View how many sessions include a cart addition, reach checkout, or result in a completed purchase, for example. Comparing these stages can reveal drop-off points along the customer journey that your A/B test can target for improvement.


### 2. Decide what to test and form a hypothesis


Use the conversion rate to establish a baseline and identify a single, measurable goal for your A/B test. This could include increasing add-to-cart rates, form completions, or visits to product pages.


Choose an element that addresses a specific barrier in the[customer journey](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-journey-map) you identified during your performance review. For example, a landing page with high form abandonment might benefit from fewer form fields, while one with high[bounce rates](https://www.shopify.com/blog/bounce-rate) could need a clearer, more prominent CTA or more relevant hero imagery.


Once you’ve chosen the element, write a clear hypothesis that identifies the proposed change, the expected outcome, and the reasoning behind it. You might hypothesize that replacing the CTA “Shop the collection” with the more time-sensitive “Shop before the sale ends” will increase[click-through rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ctr-meaning) because urgency motivates faster action.


Build your test variation around that single change, keeping other elements unchanged, and plan your sample size and test duration before starting based on your existing conversion rate and the improvement you want to detect.


### 3. Conduct your A/B test


Run your control version and modified version simultaneously, tracking specific metrics related to your hypothesis. Shopify store owners can set a control version and modified version of a landing page as live at the same time on the Grow plan or higher using[Shopify Rollouts](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/markets/rollouts) .


In your Shopify admin, go to Markets > Rollouts, click Create rollout, and select Experiment. Add your theme changes, then configure your audiences and experiment dates. Split the traffic between your existing page and modified page with a 50/50 split, making sure both versions display correctly before setting them live. Allow your test to run for your planned duration, then monitor the results.


You can also use third-party apps like[EComposer Landing Page Builder,](https://apps.shopify.com/ecomposer)[Shogun](https://apps.shopify.com/shogun-ab-testing) , and[Intelligems: A/B Testing](https://apps.shopify.com/intelligems) to run tests and handle calculations for sample size and splitting your site traffic, helping you compare page variations and assess their performance against your conversion goals.


### 4. Analyze your test results


Assess your chosen metric for both the control version and modified version of your landing page to see which performs better against your primary goal.


[Shopify reports](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/behaviour-reports#online-store-conversion-over-time) can show conversion rate, add-to-cart rate, reached checkout rate, and bounce rate for A/B tests you’ve conducted. Open your experiment under Markets > Rollouts to review its analytics. Check whether you have enough data to support a conclusion; a difference of a handful of conversions may not identify a clear winning variation.


### 5. Implement the winning version


Use the outcomes to select the more successful landing page and publish the winning variation. If your results are inconclusive, retain the existing version and develop another test.


## A/B testing for landing pages FAQ


### Can you A/B test landing pages?


You can A/B test landing pages by comparing an existing page with a modified version to see which performs better against a specific goal. Test elements like copy, images, CTAs, forms, or navigation, keeping other elements unchanged.


### How do you test a landing page?


To test a landing page, use A/B testing tools to split traffic between a control version and a modified version, then analyze your chosen metric.


### What are the types of A/B testing?


Types of A/B testing include standard A/B testing, which compares two variants, and A/B/n testing, which compares multiple variants.


### Can you A/B test on a website?


You can A/B test a website to compare versions of landing pages, product pages, homepages, and other pages. Testing page elements can help you identify variations that better encourage visitors to explore the site, add items to cart, or complete purchases.
